name: voice_reply
description: Convert text into a spoken voice note and send it to the current chat as a real audio message (not a text link). Use when the user explicitly asks for a voice note/voice message, or asks OADSON to 'say' or 'read out' something. Supports multiple accents/genders on command — default is Nigerian, but switch to American, British, or a specific gender when the user asks (e.g. 'say it in an American voice', 'use a male voice', 'butler voice'). Free — uses Microsoft Edge's neural text-to-speech service, no API key or card needed.

text.description: The text to speak. Keep it conversational — this is voice, not an essay. Long text still works but produces a long voice note.

voice_preset.description: Pick based on what the user asks for. Default 'nigerian_female' if nothing specified. 'british_male_butler' for a formal/deep British male voice — use when the user asks for a 'butler' voice or similarly formal/proper tone. If the user just says 'American voice' with no gender, pick 'american_male' or 'american_female' based on conversational context, or ask if genuinely ambiguous.

voice.description: Advanced override: an exact Edge TTS voice ID (e.g. 'en-US-ChristopherNeural') instead of a preset. Only use this if the user names a specific voice that isn't covered by voice_preset. Takes precedence over voice_preset when set.
